doc: The Last Lot at the Exchange (slug bell-at-the-exchange) — slot 5 of the journeyman-everyday-1 batch (THR-1676).
Brief: `Docs/plans/encounters/journeyman-everyday-1-brief.md`.
plotHookTaken: hook.scarcity_crisis — a thin season, one lot left on the block, and
a merchant house that wants every lot it can get. (Rolled beside it:
hook.blame_falls_on_outsiders, hook.assassination_succeeded — both pull the scene
grim, and this slot carries the batch's one pleasure.)
─── The narrator's 12 questions, answered ───────────────────────────
1 P1 arrival?      Yes: `{actor}` walks onto the exchange floor in `{location}` an
hour before the closing bell (urban, the only class).
2 P2 events?       Few cargoes came in; the floor has sold almost nothing all week;
one lot is left on the block.
3 P3 one stake?    Contest, as rolled: `{cast:buyer}` bids for a merchant house and
knows every bidder but the agent; the last bid at the bell wins.
4 ≤80 words?       Opening + step-0 spine inside budget.
5 Read aloud?      Report throughout.
6 Stated, never encoded? 'The houses treat this floor as their own' is said, not
implied by a look.
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test, or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? The lot, the bell, the buyer and the house all appear
before a card or a chip names them.
9 One named person? `{cast:buyer}` — the house buyer, both beats.
10 Stake in a sentence? 'Can a stranger outbid a merchant house on its own floor
before the bell rings?'
11 Cards verb+noun, spell-style? Yes; three specials, mechanism-stating.
12 Opening per class? `urban`, written.
─── Mechanical design block (designed before the prose) ─────────────
Crux            The last lot of a thin season is on the block, and {actor} is
bidding for it against a house buyer who knows the room.
Whose problem?  The agent's. They walked in to buy; the lot is theirs or the
house's when the bell rings.
Reach = theme?  Step 0 tests Gold and is *about* pricing a lot nobody will price
aloud. Step 1 tests Gold and is *about* the bidding itself.
Shape           Test & Consequence (two steps, carryover), composed with the
query_prize face: the prize is drawn by query, not by id.
Rolled dice     p3 contest · opposition time (the bell) · disposition n/a ·
role trespasser (the houses' floor) · scale company (a house).
Consequence hand (binding, THR-1145): `story_seed` + `omen`, recorded swap
`omen` → `possession` (see `consequenceSwap`).
`possession` — a step `rewardPool` on step 1's success half,
`{ categoryWeights: { possession: 1 }, tagFilters: ['#trade'] }`.
The prize is TAG-DRAWN, not id-named: the recipe projects onto
`{ kind: 'item_template', tags: ['#trade'] }` through rewardPool
toContentQuery (site `step_reward_pool`); the tier curve pays a
better lot on a better band, and the engine renders the drawn
item as the PRIZE chip, so no authored item chip sits beside it.
Critic 2026-09-29: the `reward_draw` effect type has no `query`
field (src/types/unifiedAction.ts), and `reward_draw` is not in
PERSISTENT_EFFECT_KINDS, so the effect route failed the Rewards
block and the systems quota; the step route is the same recipe.
`story_seed` — `encounter_seed` literal `encounter.caravan_deal`
(placeless, `inheritContext`, delay 30) on step 1's failure half:
lost at the bell, the mortal is heard of by a caravan master whose
cargo has not reached the floor. Ungated everyday gold trade whose
base prose asserts no guild or house membership (rule 31). PATH
chip `seed` on the failure and critical_failure bands.
Extra: `plant_compulsion` (trade/acquire up) on step 0's
failure half (a misread price sends them into the bidding past
sense) and on step 1's failure half (lost at the bell, and wants
the next lot).
Standing        `reputation_with` `$cast:buyer`: up on a win (a real bidder),
down on a loss (they pushed the house's price up and lost).
Cool failure?   Nobody is hurt or held. The lot goes to the house, the price the
house paid is higher for them, and the house buyer remembers.
Systems quota   cast + rewards + seeds + reputation — four.
Trait hooks     Gate: none. Variant: none. Trait-only card: none. Trait fragment:
none — the bidding reads the same for every temperament and the
compulsion is the personal consequence.
Specials        step 0 `Remember The Price` (Whisper, mind). step 1 `Cloud The
Count` (Stumble, chaos) and `Hold The Bell` (Long Game, time).
No core Boost special; no rider special (the deal supplies both).
Difficulty      gold 0.40 → gold 0.45 (brief amended: no background step above 0.45).

stakes.goal: win the last lot at the exchange before the bell
stakes.risk: push the price up and still lose the lot
stakes.won: held the last bid when the bell rang
stakes.lost: lost the last lot to the merchant house
stakes.lostBadly: drove the price up and still lost the lot

template.name: The Last Lot at the Exchange

consequenceSwap.reason: A closing bell on a thin season is a price, a bidder and a lot — nothing in it is a sign from the sky, and an omen here would be dressing bolted onto a market floor. What the scene decides is who holds the lot when the bell rings, so the consequence it owes is the tag-drawn prize on the win.

openings.urban: {actor} walks onto the exchange floor in {location} an hour before the closing bell.

steps.narrativeTemplate: Few cargoes came in this season, and almost nothing has sold all week. One lot is left on the block. The merchant houses treat the exchange as their own. {cast:buyer} bids for one of them and knows every regular bidder. Whoever holds the last bid when the bell rings takes the lot, and a house outbid on its own floor remembers who did it.
steps.successAfterimage: They worked out what the lot is worth and where they would stop.
steps.failureAfterimage: They could not put a figure on the lot and went into the bidding without one.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: They priced the lot, and {cast:buyer} saw the figure they settled on.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They priced the lot and picked out the two bidders who were only there to push the price.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: They priced the lot at twice its worth and said the figure where the room could hear.

effects.narrativeHook: They went into the bidding with no figure in mind, and they keep bidding.

nudges.name: Remember The Price
nudges.effectLine: Bring back what a lot like this one sold for last season, so they know a fair figure when they hear it.

bandProse.success: They remembered last season's figure, and it was the right one to stop at.
bandProse.near_miss: They remembered last season's figure a moment after they had named their own.
bandProse.failure: They remembered last season's figure, but in a thin season it was far too low.

steps.narrativeTemplate: The bidding opens. {cast:buyer} answers every bid with a small raise. The price passes what a lot like it fetched last season. The bell ringer already has a hand on the rope.
steps.successAfterimage: They held the last bid when the bell rang, and the lot is theirs.
steps.failureAfterimage: The bell rang on the house's bid, and the lot went to {cast:buyer}.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: The lot is theirs, at a price well past what it is worth.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They took the lot at a fair price, and the floor cheered when the bell rang.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: They drove the price up, dropped out at the last raise, and the house took the lot.

effects.narrativeHook: Lost a lot at the bell, and means to win the next one.

effects.seedLabel: A caravan master with cargo still short of the exchange hears who nearly outbid the house.

nudges.name: Cloud The Count
nudges.effectLine: Cloud the rival buyer's count of the bids, so one raise goes by unanswered.

bandProse.critical_success: {cast:buyer} lost the figure halfway through a raise, and the room laughed.
bandProse.success: {cast:buyer} checked the tally twice and let one raise pass.
bandProse.failure: {cast:buyer} lost the figure, asked the floor for it, and raised again.

nudges.name: Hold The Bell
nudges.effectLine: Slow the ringer's hand on the rope, so the bidding runs long enough for one more raise.

bandProse.success_at_cost: The ringer waited, and the extra raise was the one that cost them most.
bandProse.failure: The ringer waited, and the house used the time to raise again.
bandProse.critical_failure: The ringer waited, and the house raised twice more before the bell.

narrativeTemplates.initiation: The last lot of a thin season is on the block at the exchange, and a merchant house wants it. Whoever holds the last bid at the bell takes it home.
narrativeTemplates.success: The bell rang on their bid, and the lot is theirs.
narrativeTemplates.failure: The bell rang on the house's bid. The lot went to the house, at a higher price than it would have paid.

fallback.overview: The bell has rung and the block is empty. The floor is counting the day's takings.

changes.title: A lot, bid on
changes.detail: An hour against a house buyer teaches the gold reach.

critical_success.overview: The lot went to {actor} at a fair price. {cast:buyer} bowed to them in front of the whole floor.

changes.title: Beaten fairly
changes.causeClause: Outbid a house on its own floor
changes.detail: {cast:buyer} rates them as a serious bidder.

success.overview: The bell rang on their bid. {cast:buyer} went back to the house empty-handed.

changes.title: A bidder to watch
changes.detail: {cast:buyer} thinks better of them as a bidder now.

success_at_cost.overview: The lot is theirs, bought well past its worth, and the whole floor saw the figure.

failure.overview: The bell rang on the house's bid. The house paid more for the lot than it meant to, because of {actor}.

changes.title: The next lot
changes.detail: For a while they will chase trade and buying before anything else.

changes.title: Cargo Off the Floor
changes.detail: A caravan master with unsold cargo will hear of {actor}.

critical_failure.overview: {actor} pushed the house to its highest figure of the season, and the house still took the lot.

changes.title: Still bidding
changes.detail: For a while they will chase the next deal first.

changes.detail: A caravan master with unsold cargo will hear of {actor}.

template.description: A two-step bidding contest at a town exchange: price the last lot of a thin season, then outbid a merchant house's buyer before the closing bell. The prize is drawn by query from the #trade item family; a lost or overpaid bid leaves a lean toward the next deal.
